e: Robert Hall and Michael Woodford are awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.
Department of Homeland Security agents search the home of representative Ilhan Omar in Washington, D.C., as part of an "ongoing investigation".

Hundreds of thousands of Americans in Alabama and the Florida panhandle are without electricity after Hurricane Isaias hits the U.S. Gulf Coast. Trump cancels his intentions to attend a football match between the University of Georgia and the University of Alabama in Tuscaloosa, citing a desire not to impede emergency response operations, and declares a state of emergency in Alabama and Florida.
The American military announces that it disabled a cargo ship attempting to violate its naval blockade of Iran.
The Justice Department announces that it is probing whether major television networks breached federal antitrust laws by collectively refusing to cover the White House.

The US sanctions the International Criminal Court, stating that it will never allow the court to prosecute American soldiers. The sanctions occurred after the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to former ICC judge Navi Pillay, and Trump criticized the decision on Truth Social.

During a White House event, Trump declares that the war with Iran will "be over soon, one way or the other," suggesting that the almost eight-month-old conflict would either be resolved diplomatically or militarily.

Trump announces that he secured Russian president Vladimir Putin's agreement to release diesel into U.S. and worldwide markets, saying that this will reduce rising energy costs in the midst of the Iran war.
Trump names Katie Zacharia as the new White House press secretary, succeeding Karoline Leavitt.
Nine people are killed in a gun attack in Erie, Pennsylvania.
The US begins direct negotiations with the military junta of Myanmar while continuing sanctions against its leader, Min Aung Hlaing, for human rights violations, notably the Rohingya genocide.
The US imposes additional sanctions on Iran's shadow fleet.

Trump instructs the Pentagon to prepare military options in case active combat operations against Iran resume even as he said on that day that strikes would not renew prior to the midterm elections on November 3.
The US and Greece agree on a coordinated security framework for counterterrorism information sharing among respective law enforcement agencies.

The Wall Street Journal reports that U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle asked Republican donor Eric Deters to pay off $100,000 in credit card debt in exchange for access to the Trump administration, six days before her July 2025 Senate confirmation hearing. Guilfoyle's attorney said that any payments from Deters were for appearances.

Paramount Skydance completes its US$110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, in one of the largest media mergers in history. The deal combines two of Hollywood's largest film studios with major television and streaming businesses including CBS, CNN, HBO and Paramount+, with the combined company renamed Skydance Corporation.
Trump authorizes execution by firing squad for the Fort Hood attacker Nidal Hasan.

The Trump administration authorizes a $1 billion munitions sale to the UAE for up to 10,000 Advanced Precision Kill Weapon Systems, as well as a $400 million sale of "repair and return services" for Patriot missiles to Kuwait.
Trump states that he remains "always open" to direct negotiations with Tehran.
The US announces that foreign financial institutions doing business with Iran may be sanctioned without warning.

At a campaign rally in Nebraska, President Trump suggests that Iran could "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego while defending the economic costs of the Iran war, prompting criticism from California officials and some Republicans. The White House says his remarks were intended to highlight the threat of Iranian attacks that US military action was meant to prevent.

The State Department announces that the US "kicked out" two members of the Iranian delegation who attended the recent United Nations General Assembly after they ignored an order to leave the country long after the General Assembly had ended.

Trump withdraws all US bombers from RAF Fairford, a British air base targeted by an attack that the UK linked to the Iranian government, due to urgent concerns about a potentially complex drone attack ordered by the IRGC as part of a plot to target the aircraft and kill American soldiers at RAF Fairford, which is loosely modeled after Ukraine's Operation Spiderweb.

The FBI arrests Chinese American Wanying Zhang at Los Angeles International Airport for allegedly acting as an unregistered agent of China and surveilling the family of President of Taiwan Lai Ching-te in the United States.

Trump establishes a task force to examine the risks and opportunities of AI and recommend what role the federal government should play in overseeing the technology without compromising competitiveness with China.
The US imposes sanctions on Hamas' financing network, which includes two French-based funds.
Alabama state representative Brett Easterbrook is arrested on charges of first-degree human trafficking and prostitution as part of a sting. At least a dozen other men are arrested.

The US imposes new sanctions on Iran, targeting rail, automotive, manufacturing, and steel sectors, as well as overseas suppliers, saying that the goal is to economically isolate the Iranian government.
United States Department of the Treasury
The U.S. military starts sending about 9,000 soldiers to the Middle East on naval ships, such as the USS Makin Island amphibious readiness group and the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group.
The Trump administration concludes the withdrawal of US soldiers from their final bases in Iraq, marking the end of the US-led coalition's war against ISIL.
A US defense contract for counter-drone systems is awarded to the Israeli company SMARTSHOOTER.
Syria is removed from the US munitions export prohibition list.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirms that the American military will reduce 20% of its generals and admirals.

The United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit temporarily halts the execution of Christa Gail Pike, but the U.S. Supreme Court later allows it to proceed. Pike survives two doses of pentobarbital and is hospitalized, prompting Tennessee governor Bill Lee to suspend the state's remaining 2026 execution and order an independent review.

An immigration judge rules that Trump can deport the Palestinian-born leader of Wisconsin's largest mosque—an outspoken advocate of Palestinian rights—who does not have a criminal record in the US, where he has lived since 1993 on national security grounds, citing his imprisonment in Israel in 1988 after being convicted of throwing stones at Israeli military personnel in the West Bank.
The US sanctions ten people and entities in various jurisdictions that have acquired weapons and their parts for Iran's Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics.
United States Department of the Treasury
SpaceX's Starship achieves orbit for the first time, and deploys 26 "next generation" Starlink V3 satellites.

OpenAI announces that it will cancel the release of GPT-6.1, the next version of ChatGPT amid ongoing safety concerns. The company also issues an update on recent incidents during which its AI model hacked into other websites.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio orders that the Iranian delegation to the UN General Assembly immediately leave the country after overstaying amid stalled negotiations to end the war between both nations.

Trump says that he still expected more talks to resume with Iran during the week. Trump claims that Iran "wanted to make a deal," but they "overplayed their hand" by offering conditions that the US "would have maybe agreed to a year ago."
